path_title: Academic Pathway: High School Graduate (Senior Secondary) to Bachelor of Science in Computer Science

student_input.academic_goal: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science

academic_stages_summary: The pathway guides the student from post‑secondary preparation through university admission, foundational coursework, core computer‑science studies, research/project work, and final graduation. Each stage builds on verified academic achievements, ensuring prerequisite knowledge before advancing. The sequence aligns with typical global accreditation standards for a B.Sc. in Computer Science.

steps.title: Standardized Entrance Exam Preparation
steps.description: Prepare for and sit the required university entrance examinations (e.g., SAT, ACT, or national university entrance test). Focus on strengthening quantitative reasoning, analytical writing, and problem‑solving skills. Review high‑school mathematics, physics, and introductory programming concepts. Achieve scores that meet or exceed the target institution's minimum thresholds.
steps.completion_criteria: Obtain a minimum composite score of 1300 (SAT) or equivalent national exam percentile of 85% and secure official score reports.
key_academic_activities: Problem‑solving workshops and timed writing exercises

steps.title: Baseline Diagnostic Full-Length SAT/ACT Test
steps.description: Administer an official full-length SAT or ACT under timed conditions to establish a performance baseline across all sections.
steps.completion_criteria: Test completed and raw scores recorded; baseline percentile documented.

steps.title: Algebra I & II Concept Review
steps.description: Systematically review linear equations, quadratic functions, systems of equations, and polynomial operations using textbook chapters and problem sets.
steps.completion_criteria: Complete assigned problem set with ≥ 85% correct answers on graded rubric.

steps.title: Geometry and Trigonometry Refresher
steps.description: Cover Euclidean geometry proofs, coordinate geometry, and basic trigonometric identities through guided worksheets.
steps.completion_criteria: Score ≥ 80% on geometry quiz and submit a proof worksheet approved by instructor.

steps.title: Pre‑Calculus and Calculus Fundamentals
steps.description: Study limits, derivatives, integrals, and function transformations with emphasis on SAT/ACT applicable topics.
steps.completion_criteria: Complete calculus problem set with ≥ 85% accuracy and pass a short timed quiz.

steps.title: Linear Algebra Basics Module
steps.description: Introduce vectors, matrices, and systems of linear equations, focusing on conceptual understanding for quantitative sections.
steps.completion_criteria: Submit a worksheet solving three matrix problems with ≥ 90% correctness.

steps.title: Physics Fundamentals for Problem Solving
steps.description: Review mechanics concepts (kinematics, forces) that appear in quantitative reasoning passages.
steps.completion_criteria: Complete a set of 15 physics word‑problem questions with ≥ 80% correct.

steps.title: Introductory Programming Concepts Review (Python)
steps.description: Refresh basic programming constructs—variables, loops, functions—to support logical reasoning in test scenarios.
steps.completion_criteria: Write and successfully run three short scripts solving arithmetic puzzles.

steps.title: Timed Quantitative Reasoning Practice Set 1
steps.description: Complete a 35‑minute timed set of mixed quantitative questions mirroring SAT/ACT difficulty.
steps.completion_criteria: Achieve ≥ 75% correct under timed conditions; submit answer sheet for review.

steps.title: Timed Quantitative Reasoning Practice Set 2
steps.description: Another 35‑minute timed quantitative set focusing on advanced algebra and data analysis items.
steps.completion_criteria: Score ≥ 78% accuracy; error analysis report completed.

steps.title: Analytical Writing Workshop: Essay Structure
steps.description: Study the SAT/ACT essay rubric, learn thesis development, evidence integration, and concluding strategies through guided examples.
steps.completion_criteria: Draft an outline for a sample prompt that meets all rubric criteria.

steps.title: Timed Analytical Writing Practice Test
steps.description: Write a complete analytical essay within the 40‑minute limit on a provided prompt.
steps.completion_criteria: Essay scored ≥ 4 on the official rubric by a certified evaluator.

steps.title: Problem‑Solving Workshop: Combinatorics & Probability
steps.description: Engage in interactive problem‑solving sessions covering permutations, combinations, and basic probability models.
steps.completion_criteria: Complete workshop worksheet with ≥ 85% correct solutions.

steps.title: Full‑Length Practice Test #1 with Review
steps.description: Take a complete official practice test under exam conditions, then conduct a detailed item‑by‑item review.
steps.completion_criteria: Overall score ≥ 90% of target threshold; review document highlighting at least three improvement areas.

steps.title: Full‑Length Practice Test #2 with Review
steps.description: Second full official practice test to measure progress, followed by a comparative analysis against Test #1.
steps.completion_criteria: Score improvement of ≥ 5 points over Test #1; submit comparative analysis chart.

steps.title: Score Analysis and Target Adjustment Plan
steps.description: Analyze cumulative test data to refine target scores and allocate remaining study time to weakest sections.
steps.completion_criteria: Produce a written study plan with specific weekly goals approved by mentor.

steps.title: Final Mock Exam Under Real Conditions
steps.description: Administer a final full-length SAT/ACT mock exam in a quiet environment, replicating test day timing, breaks, and materials.
steps.completion_criteria: Achieve score meeting or exceeding the institution’s minimum threshold; submit official score report.

steps.title: University Application Portfolio Development
steps.description: Compile a comprehensive application package that includes academic transcripts, personal statement, letters of recommendation, and any required supplemental essays. Align the portfolio with the target university's admission criteria for Computer Science. Incorporate evidence of extracurricular academic activities such as coding clubs or science fairs. Submit applications before all deadlines.
steps.completion_criteria: Submission of complete applications to at least three accredited universities with confirmation receipts.
key_academic_activities: Preparing a concise portfolio of coding projects or research abstracts

steps.title: Analyze target university CS admission criteria
steps.description: Examine the official admissions webpage and program handbook to extract GPA thresholds, required coursework, and supplemental essay prompts specific to the Computer Science major.
steps.completion_criteria: Compiled a criteria matrix document covering all academic requirements and essay topics

steps.title: Obtain and verify official high school transcripts
steps.description: Request sealed transcripts from the high school registrar, confirm that all grades and course titles are accurately recorded, and calculate cumulative GPA using the university's weighting system.
steps.completion_criteria: Received official transcripts and a GPA verification sheet signed by a counselor

steps.title: Complete diagnostic assessment of math and CS fundamentals
steps.description: Take a timed practice test covering calculus, linear algebra, discrete mathematics, and introductory programming concepts to benchmark readiness for CS coursework.
steps.completion_criteria: Score of ≥85% on each subject area as recorded in the assessment report

steps.title: Draft outline for personal statement
steps.description: Create a structured outline that aligns personal motivations, academic achievements, and future goals with the values and strengths of the target CS program.
steps.completion_criteria: Approved outline document containing at least four major sections

steps.title: Write first full draft of personal statement
steps.description: Expand the approved outline into a 500‑word narrative, integrating specific examples of coding experiences and leadership in technical clubs.
steps.completion_criteria: Submitted draft meeting the 500‑word count and covering all outline sections

steps.title: Revise personal statement using rubric scoring
steps.description: Apply a university‑provided personal statement rubric to evaluate clarity, relevance, and impact; edit the draft to achieve a rubric score of at least 90%.
steps.completion_criteria: Final statement version with rubric score ≥90% documented in a scoring sheet

steps.title: Identify and request two academic recommendation letters
steps.description: Select two teachers who can attest to STEM performance, draft a formal request email, and confirm their willingness to submit letters by the deadline.
steps.completion_criteria: Received written confirmation from both recommenders with agreed submission dates

steps.title: Provide recommenders with achievement summary and CV
steps.description: Prepare a concise academic summary and updated CV highlighting GPA, AP/IB scores, coding club leadership, and competition results; send to each recommender.
steps.completion_criteria: Both recommenders acknowledge receipt of the summary and CV

steps.title: Collect signed recommendation letters
steps.description: Follow up with recommenders, obtain the final sealed letters (digital PDFs or hard copies), and verify that each letter is on official letterhead and signed.
steps.completion_criteria: Two complete recommendation letters stored in the application folder

steps.title: Curate coding project portfolio
steps.description: Select three most relevant coding projects, write a one‑page summary for each detailing problem statement, technologies used, algorithms implemented, and outcomes or metrics.
steps.completion_criteria: Portfolio PDF containing three project summaries with screenshots and GitHub links

steps.title: Draft research abstract for science fair participation
steps.description: Compose a 250‑word abstract describing the hypothesis, methodology, data analysis, and conclusions of the recent science fair project related to computational modeling.
steps.completion_criteria: Abstract approved by science fair advisor and saved as a PDF

steps.title: Write supplemental essay on diversity in tech
steps.description: Respond to the university’s prompt about fostering diversity, drawing on personal experiences in coding clubs and outreach initiatives.
steps.completion_criteria: Essay of 300‑400 words completed and edited for grammar

steps.title: Peer‑review supplemental essay with study group
steps.description: Share the draft essay with a peer group of at least three students, collect feedback using a structured review form, and incorporate suggested improvements.
steps.completion_criteria: Revised essay reflecting at least three actionable peer suggestions

steps.title: Assemble complete application package PDF
steps.description: Combine verified transcripts, final personal statement, supplemental essay, recommendation letters, project portfolio, and research abstract into a single, ordered PDF following the university’s formatting guidelines.
steps.completion_criteria: Single PDF file size ≤ 10 MB that passes the university’s upload validation test

steps.title: Conduct final checklist audit against university application list
steps.description: Use the official checklist to verify that every required document, essay prompt, and supplemental item is present and correctly labeled in the assembled PDF.
steps.completion_criteria: Signed audit sheet confirming 100 % checklist compliance

steps.title: Submit application via university portal before deadline
steps.description: Log into the admissions portal, upload the final PDF, fill out required fields, pay any application fees, and capture the confirmation receipt.
steps.completion_criteria: Official submission confirmation email with timestamp before the posted deadline

steps.title: Admission Acceptance and Enrollment
steps.description: Review admission offers, evaluate scholarship or financial aid packages, and accept the most suitable offer. Complete enrollment paperwork, tuition deposit, and registration for the first semester. Attend orientation sessions to become familiar with university policies, academic advising, and support services. Ensure all pre‑enrollment health and residency documentation is filed.
steps.completion_criteria: Receipt of official enrollment confirmation and registration for at least 12 credit hours for Semester 1.
key_academic_activities: Submission of enrollment forms and tuition deposit

steps.title: Conduct comparative analysis of admission offers
steps.description: Gather all admission letters, extract tuition, credit requirements, and program specifics. Populate a side‑by‑side spreadsheet to quantify costs, scholarship amounts, and academic resources.
steps.completion_criteria: Completed spreadsheet with all offers ranked and documented, saved in university‑approved format.

steps.title: Evaluate scholarship and financial aid packages
steps.description: Review each financial aid award letter, calculate net cost after scholarships, grants, and loans. Prepare a cost‑benefit summary for each institution.
steps.completion_criteria: Cost‑benefit summary approved by personal financial advisor and saved as PDF.

steps.title: Create decision matrix and select optimal offer
steps.description: Combine the comparative analysis and financial evaluation into a weighted decision matrix reflecting academic fit, cost, and support services.
steps.completion_criteria: Decision matrix with final selected institution highlighted and rationale documented.

steps.title: Submit formal acceptance of chosen admission offer
steps.description: Complete the official acceptance form on the university portal, sign electronically, and request confirmation of enrollment status.
steps.completion_criteria: Confirmation email from university indicating accepted status.

steps.title: Complete university enrollment portal forms
steps.description: Enter personal data, emergency contacts, and intended major into the enrollment system. Upload required identification documents.
steps.completion_criteria: All enrollment fields marked complete and system-generated receipt saved.

steps.title: Submit official transcript verification
steps.description: Order sealed transcripts from previous institutions, upload scanned copies, and request verification through the registrar’s office.
steps.completion_criteria: Verification status shown as 'Approved' in enrollment portal.

steps.title: Pay tuition deposit and obtain receipt
steps.description: Process the required deposit via the university’s payment gateway, selecting appropriate payment method and confirming transaction.
steps.completion_criteria: Official deposit receipt PDF stored in student account and email confirmation received.

steps.title: Register for first‑semester core Computer Science courses
steps.description: Log into the course registration system, select required CS101, CS102, and introductory mathematics courses, and submit the schedule for approval.
steps.completion_criteria: Course registration status displayed as 'Enrolled' for all selected classes.

steps.title: Complete prerequisite placement assessment for Mathematics 101
steps.description: Take the online diagnostic exam covering algebra and pre‑calculus topics to determine appropriate math placement.
steps.completion_criteria: Placement score posted with recommended Math 101 section and saved screenshot.

steps.title: Attend mandatory new‑student orientation session
steps.description: Participate in the live orientation webcast, complete all interactive polls, and download the orientation handbook.
steps.completion_criteria: Orientation attendance certificate downloaded and saved.

steps.title: Meet with academic advisor to draft first‑year degree plan
steps.description: Schedule a one‑on‑one meeting, discuss major requirements, and co‑create a semester‑by‑semester course map in the advising portal.
steps.completion_criteria: Approved degree plan PDF exported from advising system.

steps.title: Review and sign university policies and code of conduct
steps.description: Read the student handbook, acknowledge understanding of academic integrity, and electronically sign the compliance form.
steps.completion_criteria: Signed policy document timestamped and stored in student portal.

steps.title: Submit pre‑enrollment health immunization records
steps.description: Obtain up‑to‑date immunization proof from healthcare provider, scan, and upload to the campus health services portal.
steps.completion_criteria: Health record status updated to 'Verified' in portal.

steps.title: File residency documentation for tuition classification
steps.description: Gather lease agreement, utility bills, and state ID to prove in‑state residency, then submit through the registrar’s residency verification system.
steps.completion_criteria: Residency status changed to 'In‑State' with confirmation email.

steps.title: Set up university email account and LMS access
steps.description: Activate the @university.edu email, configure password, and log into the learning management system to enroll in course sites.
steps.completion_criteria: Successful login to LMS and receipt of welcome email.

steps.title: Create personal academic calendar with key dates
steps.description: Import university academic calendar into personal scheduling app, add registration deadlines, exam periods, and orientation events.
steps.completion_criteria: Calendar shared with advisor and screenshot of populated events saved.

steps.title: Foundational University Coursework
steps.description: Complete the first-year curriculum covering Calculus I & II, Discrete Mathematics, Introduction to Programming (Python/Java), and Academic Writing for STEM. Achieve mastery of mathematical proof techniques and algorithmic thinking. Maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 3.5 to ensure progression eligibility. Participate in laboratory sessions and tutorial groups for hands‑on reinforcement.
steps.completion_criteria: Earn a minimum of 30 credit hours with a GPA ≥ 3.5 and pass all core foundation exams with ≥ 80% score.
key_academic_activities: Calculus I & II problem sets and exams
Introductory programming labs and project submissions

steps.title: Complete Calculus I Weekly Problem Sets
steps.description: Solve all assigned problem sets covering limits, derivatives, and basic integration techniques, submitting solutions through the LMS.
steps.completion_criteria: All problem sets submitted with an average score of at least 85%.

steps.title: Calculus I Midterm Exam Preparation
steps.description: Attend review sessions, create a formula sheet, and complete a timed practice exam covering all Calculus I topics.
steps.completion_criteria: Achieve ≥ 80% on the practice exam and attend at least two review sessions.

steps.title: Calculus I Final Exam Execution
steps.description: Sit for the official Calculus I final exam, applying problem‑solving strategies learned throughout the semester.
steps.completion_criteria: Score ≥ 75% on the final exam as recorded by the registrar.

steps.title: Complete Calculus II Weekly Problem Sets
steps.description: Work through problem sets on techniques of integration, series, and multivariable concepts, uploading solutions for grading.
steps.completion_criteria: Average problem‑set score of at least 85% across all weeks.

steps.title: Calculus II Midterm Exam Preparation
steps.description: Form study groups, develop summary notes, and complete a full‑length practice midterm covering integration methods and series.
steps.completion_criteria: Practice midterm score ≥ 80% and participation in at least two group study sessions.

steps.title: Calculus II Final Exam Execution
steps.description: Take the official Calculus II final exam, demonstrating mastery of advanced integration and series convergence.
steps.completion_criteria: Achieve a final exam grade of ≥ 75%.

steps.title: Discrete Mathematics Proof Assignment 1
steps.description: Write a formal proof for the principle of mathematical induction applied to a given sequence, following course formatting guidelines.
steps.completion_criteria: Proof submitted and graded with at least 85% correctness.

steps.title: Discrete Mathematics Proof Assignment 2
steps.description: Construct a rigorous proof using combinatorial arguments for a graph theory problem provided in the syllabus.
steps.completion_criteria: Assignment returned with a minimum of 85% on the rubric.

steps.title: Discrete Mathematics Midterm Exam Preparation
steps.description: Complete a set of practice problems covering logic, set theory, and proof techniques, and attend a faculty‑led review workshop.
steps.completion_criteria: Practice problem set average ≥ 80% and attendance recorded for the workshop.

steps.title: Discrete Mathematics Final Exam Execution
steps.description: Sit for the comprehensive final exam, applying proof strategies to novel problems in discrete structures.
steps.completion_criteria: Final exam score ≥ 75% as posted on the course portal.

steps.title: Introductory Programming Lab: Syntax and Control Structures
steps.description: Complete hands‑on lab exercises in Python (or Java) focusing on variables, loops, and conditional statements, submitting code via Git.
steps.completion_criteria: All lab scripts pass automated tests with ≥ 90% correctness.

steps.title: Introductory Programming Lab: Functions and Data Structures
steps.description: Implement functions, lists, dictionaries (or arrays, ArrayLists), and perform unit testing in a series of lab assignments.
steps.completion_criteria: Lab deliverables receive a grade of at least 85% and all unit tests pass.

steps.title: Programming Project Milestone 1: Specification Draft
steps.description: Write a detailed project specification for a small software application, including requirements, design diagrams, and timeline.
steps.completion_criteria: Specification approved by the instructor with no major revisions.

steps.title: Programming Project Milestone 2: Prototype Implementation
steps.description: Develop a functional prototype implementing core features, commit code to repository, and conduct peer code review.
steps.completion_criteria: Prototype passes acceptance tests and receives ≥ 80% in peer review feedback.

steps.title: Academic Writing for STEM: Research Essay Draft
steps.description: Compose a 1500‑word essay on a current topic in computer science, integrating scholarly sources and adhering to APA style.
steps.completion_criteria: Draft submitted and receives a minimum of 85% on the writing rubric.

steps.title: GPA Monitoring and Progress Review
steps.description: Calculate cumulative GPA after each graded component, compare against the 3.5 threshold, and meet with academic advisor if below target.
steps.completion_criteria: Documented GPA report showing ≥ 3.5 and advisor meeting minutes filed.

steps.title: Core Computer Science Major Courses & Capstone Project
steps.description: Enroll in upper‑division courses such as Data Structures, Algorithms, Computer Architecture, Operating Systems, and Database Systems. Conduct a supervised capstone project that integrates theory and practice, resulting in a documented software solution or research paper. Fulfill elective requirements in areas like AI, Networks, or Software Engineering. Maintain a major‑specific GPA of at least 3.3.
steps.completion_criteria: Complete a minimum of 90 credit hours, achieve a major GPA ≥ 3.3, and successfully defend a capstone project meeting departmental rubric standards.
key_academic_activities: Capstone project proposal, implementation, and defense

steps.title: Review prerequisite lower‑division CS concepts
steps.description: Study and self‑assess programming fundamentals, discrete mathematics, and introductory computer systems to ensure readiness for upper‑division coursework.
steps.completion_criteria: Score ≥ 85% on a diagnostic quiz covering loops, recursion, proofs, and binary logic.

steps.title: Register for Data Structures (CS 210) and obtain syllabus
steps.description: Complete enrollment through the university portal, download the official syllabus, and note assessment dates and required textbooks.
steps.completion_criteria: Enrollment confirmation receipt and syllabus saved in course folder.

steps.title: Complete Data Structures weekly problem sets
steps.description: Solve assigned problem sets on linked lists, trees, and hash tables, documenting solutions and complexity analysis.
steps.completion_criteria: Submit all sets with ≥ 85% average grade as recorded in the LMS.

steps.title: Prepare for and pass Data Structures midterm exam
steps.description: Review lecture notes, complete practice exams, and attend office‑hour review sessions to master core concepts.
steps.completion_criteria: Achieve ≥ 80% score on the official midterm exam.

steps.title: Enroll in Algorithms (CS 311) and attend introductory lectures
steps.description: Secure a seat in the Algorithms course, obtain the syllabus, and attend the first three lecture sessions covering asymptotic analysis.
steps.completion_criteria: Enrollment confirmation and attendance record for lectures 1‑3.

steps.title: Submit Algorithm design assignment on divide‑and‑conquer
steps.description: Design, implement, and analyze a divide‑and‑conquer algorithm (e.g., mergesort variant) with formal correctness proof.
steps.completion_criteria: Assignment graded ≥ 90% for correctness, analysis, and code quality.

steps.title: Complete Operating Systems lab experiments
steps.description: Perform three hands‑on labs: process scheduling simulation, semaphore‑based synchronization, and virtual memory paging, each with a written report.
steps.completion_criteria: All lab reports submitted with ≥ 85% grade and lab code passes provided test suites.

steps.title: Design ER diagram for Database Systems case study
steps.description: Create a complete entity‑relationship diagram for the given business scenario, normalize to 3NF, and obtain instructor approval.
steps.completion_criteria: Approved ER diagram uploaded to the course portal.

steps.title: Select and register for AI elective (CS 340) with advisor justification
steps.description: Choose an AI elective aligned with career goals, complete the elective justification form, and secure advisor signature.
steps.completion_criteria: Advisor‑signed form and enrollment confirmation recorded.

steps.title: Draft Capstone project proposal
steps.description: Write a detailed proposal outlining problem statement, objectives, methodology, milestones, and required resources for the capstone.
steps.completion_criteria: Proposal receives faculty approval with no major revisions.

steps.title: Conduct literature review and compile annotated bibliography
steps.description: Identify, read, and summarize ten peer‑reviewed papers relevant to the capstone topic, creating an annotated bibliography.
steps.completion_criteria: Annotated bibliography submitted and accepted by the capstone supervisor.

steps.title: Implement core authentication module of capstone
steps.description: Develop, unit‑test, and document the authentication component using secure coding practices and framework guidelines.
steps.completion_criteria: All unit tests pass with ≥ 90% coverage and code review rating ≥ 4/5.

steps.title: Perform integration testing and produce test report
steps.description: Integrate all capstone modules, execute system‑level test cases, log defects, and produce a comprehensive test report.
steps.completion_criteria: Test report submitted with ≤ 5 critical defects remaining.

steps.title: Write final capstone report and prepare presentation slides
steps.description: Compose a 10‑page technical report describing design, implementation, evaluation, and future work; create a 15‑minute slide deck.
steps.completion_criteria: Report and slides approved by supervisor with no major edits.

steps.title: Defend capstone project before evaluation committee
steps.description: Deliver the oral presentation, answer committee questions, and incorporate any required revisions into the final documentation.
steps.completion_criteria: Receive a passing grade of ≥ 70% and submit final approved documents to the department repository.

steps.title: Degree Completion and Graduation
steps.description: Finalize all academic requirements, submit graduation application, and clear any outstanding administrative holds. Attend the graduation ceremony and receive the Bachelor of Science in Computer Science degree. Optionally, apply for post‑graduation academic recognitions such as honors or dean's list certification. Update academic transcripts and request official degree verification for future pursuits.
steps.completion_criteria: Official issuance of the B.Sc. in Computer Science degree and receipt of a certified transcript confirming completion of all program requirements.

steps.title: Review Graduation Eligibility Checklist
steps.description: Examine the university's graduation eligibility criteria, confirming completion of all required credit hours, core courses, and elective requirements for the B.S. in Computer Science.
steps.completion_criteria: Signed eligibility confirmation form uploaded to the student portal with zero outstanding items.

steps.title: Finalize Capstone Project Documentation
steps.description: Prepare the final written report, architecture diagrams, and user manual for the senior capstone software project, adhering to the department's formatting standards.
steps.completion_criteria: Report PDF approved by the capstone advisor and stored in the designated repository.

steps.title: Submit Capstone Code Repository and Demonstration Video
steps.description: Upload the complete source code, build scripts, and a 10‑minute demonstration video to the university's code archive system.
steps.completion_criteria: Repository receives a 'Submission Complete' status and passes automated integrity checks.

steps.title: Prepare for Comprehensive Final Exam
steps.description: Create a study schedule covering algorithms, operating systems, databases, and software engineering, and complete practice problem sets from prior semesters.
steps.completion_criteria: Achieve ≥ 85% average on three timed practice exams.

steps.title: Take Comprehensive Final Exam
steps.description: Sit for the department‑administered comprehensive exam that tests mastery of core computer science concepts required for graduation.
steps.completion_criteria: Receive a final exam score of at least 70% as recorded in the exam results portal.

steps.title: Request Academic Reference Letters from Advisors
steps.description: Contact the undergraduate advisor and capstone supervisor to obtain two formal reference letters supporting post‑graduation opportunities.
steps.completion_criteria: Both letters received as PDF files signed and uploaded to the career services portal.

steps.title: Submit Graduation Application via Student Portal
steps.description: Complete the online graduation application, confirming personal information, degree intent, and ceremony attendance preferences.
steps.completion_criteria: Application status changes to 'Submitted' with a confirmation email receipt.

steps.title: Conduct Final Transcript Audit with Registrar
steps.description: Schedule a meeting with the registrar's office to verify that all courses, grades, and transfer credits are accurately reflected on the official transcript.
steps.completion_criteria: Registrar issues an 'Audit Cleared' certificate attached to the student record.

steps.title: Resolve Outstanding Grade Appeals
steps.description: File any necessary grade appeal forms for courses with disputed marks and attend the required review meetings.
steps.completion_criteria: All appealed grades are finalized and reflected in the transcript audit report.

steps.title: Clear Financial and Library Holds
steps.description: Pay any remaining tuition balances, settle library fines, and verify that the student account shows a zero‑balance status.
steps.completion_criteria: Student account status displays 'No Holds' in the financial services portal.

steps.title: Obtain Dean's List Certification (if eligible)
steps.description: Submit a request for official Dean's List recognition based on cumulative GPA meeting the honors threshold.
steps.completion_criteria: Dean's List certificate issued and added to the academic record.

steps.title: Apply for Honors Distinction (cum laude, magna, summa)
steps.description: Complete the honors application form, providing GPA evidence and a brief reflective essay on academic achievements.
steps.completion_criteria: Honors designation confirmed and recorded on the official transcript.

steps.title: Order Official Diploma and Verify Printing Details
steps.description: Enter name spelling, degree title, and honors notation into the diploma ordering system, then review the proof for accuracy.
steps.completion_criteria: Printed diploma order receives 'Approved' status and expected delivery date.

steps.title: Attend Commencement Rehearsal
steps.description: Participate in the mandatory rehearsal, learning the procession order, seating arrangement, and diploma receipt protocol.
steps.completion_criteria: Rehearsal attendance logged and signed off by the ceremony coordinator.

steps.title: Participate in Graduation Ceremony and Collect Diploma
steps.description: Walk the commencement stage, receive the diploma from the university official, and attend the post‑ceremony reception.
steps.completion_criteria: Diploma physically received and ceremony participation recorded in the graduation registry.

500_steps.practical_feasibility: Theoretical Maximum with Tiered Fallback (~8-12 min)

1000_steps.practical_feasibility: Requires Enterprise Quota (>8k TPM) or Extended Async Queue (~18-25 min)

architecture_analysis.key_1_responsibility: Primary Academic Pathway, Macro Milestones, Dependency Ordering, Prerequisites
architecture_analysis.key_2_responsibility: Parallel Milestone Expansion, Granular Micro/Nano Subtasks, Academic Blindspot Detection
architecture_analysis.bottleneck_identified: Groq 8,000 TPM shared organization token ceiling is the primary constraint. Mitigated via dual-key parallel batching, compact JSON schemas, and fast-model fallback.
